newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt's Tarr resigns as chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt's Tarr resigns as chief executive.

text.p: Harcourt General Inc. said Tuesday that Robert Tarr Jr. was resigning as president, chief executive and chief operating officer of the company, whose operations include the posh Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman department stores and publisher Harcourt Brace.
Tarr, 53, whose resignation will take effect Jan. 15, will resign identical positions at the Neiman Marcus Group Inc., the Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman unit 53 percent owned by Harcourt.
Harcourt Chairman Richard Smith, 72, will assume the duties of chief executive of both companies, Harcourt said.

Richard Smith's 37-year-old son, Robert Smith, and his son-in-law, Brian Knez, 39, will become presidents and co-chief operating officers at Harcourt General. Robert Smith will also become president and chief operating officer at Neiman Marcus, the company said.
Robert Smith and Knez are currently group vice presidents at Harcourt.
Tarr said both companies were in strong financial position, making it an appropriate time to implement a management succession plan. Tarr, 53, has been chief executive at both companies since 1991.

"After 20 years of rewarding service with this company, the last five as chief executive officer, this is also an opportunity for me to take some time off and enjoy my family before moving on to new challenges," Tarr said in a statement. Harcourt General is based in Chestnut Hill, Mass.
